verdict.rationale: cubic's docs state that once installed it automatically reviews new pull requests, comments on bugs and improvements, and re-reviews new changes after force-pushes. Context comes from learnings mined from senior reviewers' historical comments and from cross-repo checks of shared APIs and schemas, and community users note the comments are contextualized and have become quieter and more useful. missing for 10: rigorous independent hands-on evidence of review-comment accuracy (community feedback is brief and anecdotal), and PRs opened before installation need a manual trigger.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get automatic code review with contextual feedback on every pull request

citations.quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.
Comments on bugs and improvements in pull requests
cubic now reviews the new changes after a force-push when it can safely compare them with a previously reviewed version.
cubic analyzes their historical PR comments to extract learnings from the patterns they consistently enforce.
Link related repositories so reviews can check shared APIs, schemas, docs, or release work.
I've been testing this for the last few months, and it is now much quieter than before, and even more useful.
